title: DR1 shows "Not applicable" against a question the notification never had to answer; the frontend shows "Not provided", which reads as an omission.

finding.frontend: Every blank value on the review page renders as "Not provided" — three times on the captured page, against Region of origin code, Internal reference number and Number of packages. It is one string, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:3, applied by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/rows/value-text.js:15-17 to any value the answer model treats as blank, whatever the reason it is blank. "Not provided" reads as a reproach: it tells the user something was expected of them and they did not do it, even where the question never applied.
finding.prototype: DR1 renders the same rows as "Not applicable" — app/routes.js:4065-4070 — which says the opposite: the question had no bearing on this notification and no action is owed. DR1 keeps a separate treatment, an empty value marked "Missing", for a value the service actually still needs, and uses it only inside a card the error summary has already flagged. So the two cases a user can be in are told apart by the words on the page.
finding.difference: Replace the single "Not provided" string with "Not applicable" for a question that did not apply, in both the English and Welsh copy. Keep it distinct from the missing-value treatment that the incomplete review state introduces, so the page never uses one form of words for both a question that was never asked and one that still needs an answer.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding "Not applicable" rendered against any blank row on the frontend review page.

relatedTo.why: the incomplete state introduces the missing-value treatment this placeholder has to be distinguished from
